title: onprem-airgap-offline-bundle-vendor-rke2-alpine-support
author: Alex Chen
release_notes: Add Alpine Linux support to on-prem airgap offline bundles for RKE2. Includes vendor manifests, packaging tweaks, TUF metadata updates, and docs. Customers running Alpine nodes can now use vendored offline bundles and automated bundle generation.
description: Motivation: several enterprise customers run Alpine-based nodes in air-gapped clusters and require vetted vendor bundles for RKE2 that account for musl/glibc differences, init/systemd nuances, and kernel module packaging. This PR adds Alpine as a first-class vendor target for onprem offline bundles and updates tooling to produce Alpine-compatible artifacts. Summary of changes: 1) vendor manifest and bundle layout for rke2/alpine; 2) packaging scripts -> use apk-based init wrapper and adjust rke2-*-service units to handle musl; 3) container image list and OCI tar packaging adapted to alpine-friendly base images; 4) TUF metadata generation updates and signing keys; 5) helm chart tweaks to tolerate musl-related liveness probes; 6) terraform module examples for installing offline bundles on alpine nodes; 7) comprehensive docs and upgrade/rollback notes. Checklist: [x] bundle generation automation updated and unit-tested; [x] TUF signing pipeline adjusted and smoke-tested in staging; [x] e2e airgap test harness run against local registry (flaky on image-pull in one run, retried); [x] docs updated with step-by-step offline install and rollback for alpine; [x] Linear/issue refs added (ENG-2203, INF-1987). Not included: broader distro refactors (separate PR). Related: SUP-3421. Merge note: squash-merged after addressing reviewers' comments and two CI reruns.

scripts: adapt bundle generator for apk and alpine image lists

notes: This change was intentionally scoped to Alpine-specific packaging and docs. Follow-up work will consolidate vendor commonalities across bundles. Incidentally fixed a flake in the airgap e2e harness (registry tls race) while iterating.
